source.title: Flash Multi-Head Feed-Forward Network
source.authors: Minshen Zhang; Xiang Hu; Jian-Guo Li; Wei Wu; Kewei Tu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and table formatting are flattened, but the reported loss comparisons are assignable.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares validation loss across different FFN architectures at approximately matched model sizes, bearing on whether architecture details change loss only slightly. It does not reproduce or fit the scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are architecture comparisons using PG19 validation loss. The paper does not fit power laws, test extrapolation from smaller runs, or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its downstream benchmark, speed, and memory results do not measure the architecture-sensitivity claim.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture paper proposing FlashMHF. It reports its own module against a SwiGLU baseline and ablations at roughly matched sizes (128M, 370M, 1.3B). It does not fit or test power laws, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or the shape-insensitivity claim. It uses Kaplan et al.'s finding that the FFN ratio should stay within a range as a design rationale, and does not test that finding. The comparisons swap module types and adjust depth to match parameters (e.g. 24 vs 20 vs 21 layers), so they do not isolate shape at fixed parameter count as V4 names it. The rows are the study's own method compared with others.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that FlashMHF beats the SwiGLU FFN baseline on PG19 loss and downstream averages at 128M–1.3B, with dh=128 best. Naive MH-FFN stops being competitive beyond about 128M, which they attribute to an imbalanced dff/dh ratio. They add that FlashMHF cuts peak memory 3-5x and speeds inference up to 1.08x.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and compares alternative FFN architectures and reports validation loss; it does not perform scaling-law fits, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss varies with FFN architecture and, for FlashMHF, head dimension; the study also reports different outcomes at 128M, 370M, and 1.3B.

fits_no_version.finding: At roughly matched parameter counts, swapping the SwiGLU FFN for multi-head FFN variants changes PG19 validation loss by at most about 0.05. Exceptions: Dense-MoE +0.032 at 370M, and PKV (softmax over parameter keys) +0.30. Varying FlashMHF head dimension shifts loss by up to 0.056 at 1.3B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed parameter count, replacing the FFN module type changes loss by small amounts, except for softmax-based parameter-attention substitutes.

record.problems: The study reports only three model scales and does not fit scaling curves. Model sizes are approximately, not exactly, matched; the training-token counts differ between the 1.3B and smaller runs. No uncertainty estimates are stated, and some 128M loss values are available only in a figure.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream task scores, speed, and memory results were not included because they do not measure V4's loss-sensitivity outcome. No rows were omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No loss-vs-parameters/tokens/compute power-law fit; only three scales with differing token counts.
No controlled depth/width/aspect-ratio sweep at fixed parameter count; only module swaps and head-dimension tuning of the proposed module.
Downstream scores are reported per model; no test of predictability from scale or loss.
No fitting choices or exponent comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan et al. is cited only to justify keeping the FFN ratio in an 'optimal range'. Model sizes are only approximately matched, through changed layer counts. The 1.3B runs use 100B tokens vs 60B for smaller sizes. There are no uncertainty estimates and single runs per configuration.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or test of loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
No predictions from smaller runs are compared with larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or fitted growth trends for parameters and tokens.
Tests selected FFN architecture variants at approximately matched sizes, not a broad range of depth, width, and architecture choices.
Only language-model pretraining is reported; no other modality or training regime is tested.
Downstream scores are reported, but the study does not test whether they improve predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
No scaling-law fitting choices, exponent variation, or bending of fitted scaling curves is tested.

rows.subject: MH-FFN (dh=128)
rows.operation_detail: Train a Transformer with the baseline SwiGLU FFN replaced by MH-FFN.
rows.note: The text states that this and FlashMHF outperform the SwiGLU baseline, but the figure-only values do not establish the size of the difference.
rows.check: Own-method comparison against the baseline, readable only from a figure. It is a module-type swap with depth changed (10 vs 12 layers), not a shape variation at fixed parameters.

rows.subject: FlashMHF-128hdim
rows.operation_detail: Train a Transformer with the baseline SwiGLU FFN replaced by FlashMHF.
rows.note: The text states that this and MH-FFN outperform the SwiGLU baseline, but the figure-only values do not establish the size of the difference.
rows.check: Own-method (FlashMHF) vs baseline, figure only. Not a test of V4 shape-insensitivity.

rows.subject: PKV (dh=128)
rows.operation_detail: Train a Transformer with the SwiGLU FFN replaced by the Parametric KV baseline.
rows.note: The paper describes PKV as performing notably poorly compared with the baseline.
rows.check: PKV replaces the SwiGLU FFN with softmax attention over parameters, a different module rather than a depth/width/shape choice. The 0.30 loss rise (3.334 vs 3.030) does not bear on V4; 'reversed' was an overreach.

rows.subject: MH-FFN (dh=128)
rows.operation_detail: Train a Transformer with the baseline SwiGLU FFN replaced by MH-FFN.
rows.note: The value is close to the SwiGLU baseline; the paper says naïve MH-FFN is no longer competitive at 370M.
rows.check: Naive MH-FFN vs baseline, 3.031 vs 3.030. This is a module-design ablation with depth adjusted (20 vs 24 layers), not V4's shape claim.

rows.subject: Dense-MoE
rows.operation_detail: Train the FFN sub-network variant with the number of heads set to 1.
rows.note: The paper identifies Dense-MoE as a control for whether gains come from the multi-head design or parallel FFN sub-networks.
rows.check: Dense-MoE control (H=1) vs baseline, 3.062 vs 3.030. Ablation of the authors' design, not a V4 test.

rows.subject: FlashMHF (dh=64)
rows.note: The paper says this configuration underfits and performs worse than the baseline.
rows.check: FlashMHF head-dimension ablation, 3.046 vs 3.030. Hyperparameter tuning within the proposed method; params and depth are not held strictly fixed.

rows.subject: FlashMHF (dh=128)
rows.note: The paper reports this as the best-performing 370M head-dimension setting.
rows.check: Own-method best setting, 3.014 vs 3.030. Method-vs-baseline result, not a V4 test.

rows.subject: FlashMHF (dh=256)
rows.note: The paper describes this setting as outperforming the baseline, with diminishing returns relative to dh=128.
rows.check: Own-method head-dimension ablation, 3.029 vs 3.030. Not a V4 test.

rows.subject: FlashMHF (dh=64)
rows.note: The paper reports dh=128 as the best setting at this scale.
rows.check: Own-method head-dimension ablation at 1.3B, 2.849 vs 2.843. Not a V4 test.

rows.subject: FlashMHF (dh=128)
rows.note: The paper reports this as the best 1.3B setting.
rows.check: Own-method best setting at 1.3B, 2.793 vs 2.843 (20 vs 24 layers). Method-vs-baseline result.

rows.subject: FlashMHF (dh=256)
rows.note: The paper reports dh=128 as the best setting at this scale.
rows.check: Own-method head-dimension ablation at 1.3B, 2.799 vs 2.843. Not a V4 test.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
